# bench/h264 — simulation benches

Icarus Verilog (`iverilog -g2012`) and Verilator. Every bench and runner follows the
discipline MiSTer_DVD earned the hard way and MiSTer_UMD_Video kept (its
`docs/hw_budget_and_lessons.md` §4 is the long form, reproduced in this repository's; the
rules are repeated in `CLAUDE.md` "Lessons carried"):

- **A runner `cd`s to the repository root** and every path is relative to it. `$readmemh`
  paths in the RTL assume the same.
- **Benches `$fatal(1)` on failure and print `PASS: <bench>` on success.** A `$finish` on
  the failure path exits 0 and a runner reads it as a pass. Runners require the PASS
  marker positively; they never score on the absence of "FAIL".
- **Score with `!==`, never `!=`.** An X passes `!=` vacuously. When a bench reports a count
  of zero for something that cannot be zero, suspect this first.
- **A new port on a shared module floats Z in every bench that instantiates it** without
  the port. Tie it off in every bench in the same commit.
- **`--red` proves the bench can fail.** Each runner applies deliberate mutations to a COPY
  of the shipping RTL (never the tree) and requires each to be caught by the arm written
  for it. A mutation nothing catches means the bench cannot see that defect; a mutation
  everything catches says nothing about which arm is load-bearing. Anchors are asserted
  unique so a moved line is a harness failure, not a silent no-op. **Compile a mutant
  from inside its copy** when the RTL `include`s anything: iverilog resolves
  `` `include "h264/..." `` against the working directory before any `-I` (three UMD arms
  "survived" that way).
- **Golden models** live in `tools/*_ref.py` and are regenerated at run time, never
  committed as outputs. A model written from the RTL shares its bugs: prefer an
  independent oracle (ffmpeg, the JM reference decoder, the spec) where one exists.
- **Fixtures** are one hex byte per line (`$readmemh`), with a `<stem>.meta.hex` beside them
  for parameters. Streams are made at run time (x264 through ffmpeg) or taken from the
  H.264.1 conformance set in `$H264_REFS_DIR`; generated files go to
  `bench/h264/fixtures/gen/` (gitignored). Never commit media, and never commit a
  captured stream of someone else's content.
- **Never edit a runner, its bench, or the RTL it copies while it runs** (bash reads a
  script incrementally; `--red` copies the live tree at mutation time). A log that does
  not end in `== ALL GREEN ==` or `== FAILURES ==` is a truncated run, not a result.
- **Delete the compiled sim before building it.** iverilog leaves the previous binary in
  place when a build fails, and a runner that checks `[ -f .sim/x_sim ]` then runs the
  LAST netlist and reports GREEN on it (found 2026-09-28: `run_intra_pred.sh` printed
  GREEN on an RTL edit that did not compile; its mutants, built fresh, all failed as
  "harness failure"). Every runner `rm -f`s its binary first.
- **Scratch** (`.sim/`) is gitignored. Compiled sims, logs and rendered frames go there.

| Runner | Gates |
|---|---|
| `run_display_policy.sh` | `display_policy_tb`: each explicit output profile, automatic 59.94/exact-60 selection, playback-only 50/60 match before the first picture, idle restoration, and safe fallback for an invalid profile. |
| `run_display_240_map.sh` | `display_240_map_tb`: 240p/288p physical rows map to even rows of the logical 480/576 canvas, repeated dots map to the same pixel, frame wrap has no field toggle, and 480p mapping is unchanged. |
| `run_cavlc.sh [--red] [--quick]` | the client library's CAVLC -> CABAC rewriter (`hps/lib/h264ring_cavlc.c`, fj#20, `docs/cavlc.md`), host only: per fixture [pixels] ffmpeg's frame MD5s original == rewrite, [refyuv] the conformance reference YUVs, [model] `tools/cavlc_check.py` (the project's CABAC model decodes the rewrite; bins equal; 7.4.2.10's bin limit; the SPS / PPS rules), [engines] the byte engine == the spec's, [verdict] refusals / errors by name, [pass] CABAC byte for byte, [cover] the synthetic paths reached. Fixtures: x264 (ultrafast, Baseline, High 8x8, B, slices, QP 4; MBAFF / 4:2:2 refused; CABAC passed), JM lencod (fields, Intra_8x8, B), `tools/cavlc_synth.py` (all-zero 8x8 blocks, `cabac_zero_words`, I_PCM; redundant / DP / an invalid code; ASO and truncation), every AVCv1 stream (`--quick`: a dozen); [tables] the PDF / generator checks. 30 mutations, each caught by its own arm. ~3 min full, ~2 min `--quick --red` |
| `run_scaffold.sh [--red]` | `sync_gen_tb` (the 480p raster, measured against CEA-861 figures written independently of the module), `idle_bars_tb` (every dot scored from `de_out`'s own count: the bars in EIA-189-A order, the band black but for one 32x32 marker, the marker's step and wrap, `vis = 0` black, DE delayed by exactly LAT; built twice -- STEP 4, and STEP 64 so a wrap is seen in 14 frames), `tools/check_emu_wiring.py` (the sys_top port set, ram2, clocks, ALSA off; since P3 the HPS interface's reader and status block (P2's ES stand-in retired), the decoder's and the display's seams, the lock-only DDR3 resets, the LAT-4 output stage), `tools/lint_undriven.sh`; 47 mutations (S1-S2 raster, B1-B7 idle screen, W1-W37 wiring -- each caught by its OWN named check, not merely by the checker -- L1 lint). P6: `sync_gen_il_tb`, both raster benches also at `+std=1` (60.00 Hz: 450,000 dots, the hsync edges within a dot of the uniform grid) and `+std=2` (576p / 576i); S3-S14, W38-W53 (the raster standard, anti-twitter, Refresh Rate's Auto); W54-W55 (0.4), W56 (0.5: the pause's `disp_frz` into recon_dpb); W57-W59 (0.6); W60-W68 (0.9: the overlay plane's session gate, lock-only resets, ram2 master B, the composite after the selection -- the output stage LAT 6 -- the anti-twitter choice, the raster). W111 (issue #11): HDMI's Auto aspect 16:9 under Analog Aspect Fit. ~2 min with `--red` |

Harvested from MiSTer_UMD_Video at `cc595c6` (Phase 2, `docs/harvest.md`), with the disc
arms replaced by H.264.1 streams or dropped (never left to SKIP). Conformance arms need
`$H264_REFS_DIR` (`docs/references.md`) and SKIP without it; x264 arms need ffmpeg with
libx264. `docs/h264_frontend.md`, `h264_recon.md`, `display.md` are the design notes.
